question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched authority as CCP General Secretary, state president, and Central Military Commission chairman underpins the near-95% trader consensus against his removal before 2027. Recent military leadership investigations and personnel shifts have consolidated rather than challenged his dominance, while ongoing public engagements, policy continuity on security and self-reliance priorities, and preparations for the 21st Party Congress in 2027 signal stable elite alignment. Historical precedent shows major leadership transitions cluster around scheduled congresses rather than sudden ousters. Realistic but low-probability shifts could still arise from an unforeseen health event, a severe domestic economic crisis eroding internal support, or an external crisis fracturing elite cohesion before the resolution window closes.

eventMetadata.context_description: A crowded early field for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination features no declared candidates and wide variance between national polls and prediction markets as of mid-August 2026. Trader consensus on Polymarket places Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in the lead at 23.4 percent implied probability, followed closely by Governor Gavin Newsom at 15 percent and Senator Jon Ossoff at 14.3 percent, with former Vice President Kamala Harris at 7.4 percent. Markets appear to price momentum from recent progressive primary victories, Ocasio-Cortez’s consistent polling strength in early states such as New Hampshire, and her repeated refusal to rule out a bid, while discounting Harris after the 2024 outcome and applying a premium to senators and governors with national profiles. Newsom’s position has softened amid resurfaced personal controversies and state-level challenges. The tight clustering among the top three reflects an open timeline until after the 2026 midterms, when endorsements, fundraising, and formal announcements could begin separating contenders based on coalition strength and early-state performance.

Trader consensus on Polymarket places Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in the lead at 23.4 percent implied probability, followed closely by Governor Gavin Newsom at 15 percent and Senator Jon Ossoff at 14.3 percent, with former Vice President Kamala Harris at 7.4 percent. Markets appear to price momentum from recent progressive primary victories, Ocasio-Cortez’s consistent polling strength in early states such as New Hampshire, and her repeated refusal to rule out a bid, while discounting Harris after the 2024 outcome and applying a premium to senators and governors with national profiles. Newsom’s position has softened amid resurfaced personal controversies and state-level challenges. The tight clustering among the top three reflects an open timeline until after the 2026 midterms, when endorsements, fundraising, and formal announcements could begin separating contenders based on coalition strength and early-state performance.
